key_insight: Kidney-adapted AI predicted spatial gene expression from routine histology, linking tissue appearance to disease-associated molecular programs.
clinical_relevance: Virtual molecular profiling could extend research on kidney injury and function to archived biopsies without additional spatial transcriptomics assays.
method: Adapted DeepSpot-M using paired histology and Visium data from 209 KPMP participants.
Evaluated held-out human biopsies and injury associations in 567 rats without rat-specific training.
Generated 5.46 million virtual spots from 1,534 slides across 476 additional KPMP participants.
evidence_signal: Mean gene-expression correlation doubled from 0.22 to 0.43 for each model’s 1,000 best-predicted genes; predictions preserved all 13 tested disease-marker differences and all 11 measured eGFR associations.
watch_item: These predicted molecular profiles require prospective clinical validation and should not be treated as measured gene expression or established diagnostic tests.
paper_title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
